title: Catchment and stream network of the Bagmati River above the Chobhar gorge, Nepal

headline.label: catchment of the Bagmati River above the Chobhar gorge

data: NASADEM_HGT version 001 by NASA JPL (2020): 1 arc-second (about 30 m) elevations from the SRTM flight of 11 to 22 February 2000, reprocessed by NASA, in metres above the EGM96 geoid, tiles n27e085.
method: Read a 45 × 38 km window and reprojected it to 30 m cells in EPSG:32645 by bilinear resampling.
Conditioned the terrain with priority-flood depression filling and derived D8 flow directions and upstream area (pyflwdir), with flow leaving at the window edge.

Placed the outlet on the Bagmati River at 85.2925, 27.6635 and moved it downstream to the first cell draining at least 20 km² (1149 m), then delineated the catchment above it and checked that it does not touch the window edge.
Streams: every cell draining 1 km² or more, ordered by Strahler; drainage density recounted at 0.5 and 5 km² to show the effect of the threshold.
limits: Terrain analysis for a hydrology study, not a hydrology or flood study: no rainfall, runoff, discharge or flood level is computed. NASADEM records the surface of February 2000 with about 30 m cells; SRTM-based heights carry absolute errors of about 5 to 9 m (90% level, Rodríguez et al. 2006), more on steep slopes, and include tree canopy and buildings, so streams are least reliable in forest, in towns and on flat ground.
